text:
jordan_windermere: Hey team — our prod users at Windermere are seeing p95/p99 spikes on chat completions and embeddings since ~09:00UTC. Some requests > 6s, previously < 300ms. Can you check?

sam_huynh: sorry to hear — can you drop a request id and which API (chat vs embeddings) and model?

jordan_windermere: request-id 01H8Q2X7-wn1, embeddings endpoint /v1/embeddings, model: redwood-embed-1.0, region: us-west-2, tenant_id T-3421. Happening across multiple users.

maria_garcia: noting — I see a cluster of long tail in prometheus for host gpu-node-44 around that time, GPU util ~98% and queue depth spiking.

eli_khan: can you repro with curl? also include x-redwood-debug header if possible.

jordan_windermere: repro curl attached:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "X-Request-ID: 01H8Q2X7-wn1"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1.0","input":"sample text to embed"}'
```

ops_bot: Incident created — #INC-2201203456, severity: P2, owner: @sam_huynh. Traces linked.

oncall_beth: I pulled the trace for 01H8Q2X7-wn1 — long queuing time (~4.1s) before tokenization. Downstream compute only ~200ms. Looks like per-tenant queueing.

sam_huynh: thanks Beth. that points to noisy-tenant behavior. any recent traffic spike for T-3421?

maria_garcia: yes — at 08:55UTC they started a bulk embed job (large batch requests, size ~500 per call) — our autoscaler didn't kick because requests came as rapid sequential calls and saturated per-GPURequestQueue.

eli_khan: reproduction plan: 1) capture full request trace for next 30m, 2) temporarily apply per-tenant throttle for T-3421 to restore p95, 3) propose reservation/allowlist for them or suggest rate-limit backoff.

jordan_windermere: we need minimal disruption for customers — can you do a softer throttle and a quick mitigation?

sam_huynh: propose temporary soft-throttle: reduce concurrent requests from that tenant to 8 and enforce burst token bucket with 1 req/s refill. Should bring p95 down quickly. Also offer them a reserved capacity option.

maria_garcia: I can push throttle policy now. applying to tenant T-3421 on us-west-2 host pool.

ops_bot: Policy update applied: throttle(T-3421) concurrent=8, burst=4, refill=1s.

jordan_windermere: ping when p95 improves. thanks.

maria_garcia: immediate metric check — p95 dropped from 5.9s -> 420ms within 2 minutes. p99 still a hair elevated (~1.1s) but trending down.

eli_khan: followups: 1) collect full batch size histogram for T-3421 and recommend embedding batch-size cap (<=128) or client-side chunking, 2) offer to route their heavy batch traffic to a reserved pool (Dedicated) or lower-cost quantized model (redwood-embed-1.0-q4) for throughput, 3) add tenant to short-term allowlist for reservation if they opt in.

jordan_windermere: they prefer not to move models right now. Can you send a short doc we can share with their infra team about best-practices (batch caps + retry/backoff)?

sam_huynh: will do. also adding a temporary reservation offer: 2x reserved slots in us-west-2 for next 48h at no-charge while they stabilize.

oncall_beth: logging action items: 
- [sam] send best-practices doc + template throttle settings to Jordan.
- [maria] keep throttle in place and monitor p99 for 24h; increase if necessary.
- [eli] capture traces and a heatmap of per-tenant queue times; attach to ticket.

jordan_windermere: thanks all, their infra team asked for exact headers to include for faster diagnosis.

eli_khan: ask them to send X-Request-ID, X-Client-Timestamp, and include ?trace=1 param for SDK calls. Example: 

```bash
# sdk example (python)
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="...")
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="redwood-embed-1.0", input="...", debug=True)
# ensure headers: X-Request-ID, X-Client-Timestamp
```

maria_garcia: quick note — we saw some KV-cache churn on gpu-node-44 when big batches hit; recommend adding a warm-cache guidance: avoid extreme batch sizes on latency-sensitive endpoints.

jordan_windermere: ok will pass to their team. any chance of an automated allowlist for predictable large-batch jobs?

sam_huynh: yes — we can set up a scheduled reservation window (e.g., nightly bulk embed) or whitelist job IPs with a higher reservation and separate capacity pool. that'll avoid affecting interactive traffic.

ops_bot: Ticket #INC-2201203456 updated: mitigation applied (soft-throttle), p95 improved, next update in 4 hours.

jordan_windermere: appreciate the fast response and the temporary reservation offer.

sam_huynh: I'll draft the best-practices and reservation proposal and post in this thread for Jordan to share.

eli_khan: once Jordan confirms, we should schedule a follow-up call with Windermere infra and product to discuss long-term Dedicated option.

maria_garcia: monitoring alert set: if p99 > 1.5s for 10m, page oncall.

jordan_windermere: confirmed — they accepted the temporary reservation. will coordinate with you for the follow-up call. thanks team :thumbsup:

sam_huynh: closing loop — keep this thread for follow-ups, and I'll attach the doc here shortly.

ops_bot: Incident #INC-2201203456 set to monitoring.
